findings.why_it_matters: 12.3.8.4 General rule 11 is a three-alternative cascade (a / b / c) exactly parallel to General rule 10 for program prototypes, which the markdown does render as three items. Here the third alternative is swallowed into the text of the second, so a reader (or a tool parsing the rule list) sees GR 11 as having only two sub-rules and reads 'otherwise, c) the details are taken from the external repository' as continuation prose of rule b) rather than as the independent fallback rule that governs function resolution from the external repository. The page-339 markdown slice consequently opens at item 12), leaving no item c) anywhere in the list.
findings.suggested_repair: Split at 'otherwise,' and re-emit the tail as its own list item at the same indent as a) and b), placed after the page-339 anchor to match the PDF page break: '    c) the details are taken from the external repository for the function with the same name as the externalized name of the function prototype. That function is the one that will be activated.'

findings.why_it_matters: The three NOTEs are emitted flush left instead of indented under rule 6), detaching them from their parent rule. The transcription's own convention elsewhere in this same subsection keeps rule-scoped notes indented (see page 346 'NOTE  As described in 13.4.5 ...' and page 354 'NOTE 1 / NOTE 2' under 12.4.5.8.4 General rule 1), both indented three spaces), so a reader scanning 12.4.6.3.4 cannot tell whether these notes qualify rule 6) or the whole General rules clause.
findings.suggested_repair: Indent the three NOTE paragraphs by three spaces so they sit inside list item 6), matching the treatment of the notes on pages 346 and 354.
